title: Hidden Multipliers: reposition for value, pick frameworks that fit, and what AI can't replace
summary: Jason Cohen explains how repositioning a product around more of a positive outcome (not less of a negative) can multiply price up to 10x. He covers deciding under uncertainty, why frameworks rarely transplant into a company's culture, and which jobs and products AI will and won't automate.

principles.text: Reposition from saving a cost to creating more of something customers already value; you can often charge 10x.
principles.quote: almost all products like that can be repositioned so that you're selling more value, more transformation, more of something positive that they value rather than less of a negative thing they'd like to go away.

principles.text: Pitch 'double the leads at the same cost per lead' instead of 'half the cost'; same product, far bigger price ceiling.
principles.quote: by p pitching it as double the number of leads at the same price per lead I can 10x or okay 8x in this case whatever the the price of the product same product

principles.text: Under uncertainty, anchor on what will still be true in 10 years and treat AI as part of the solution, not the problem.
principles.quote: AI is part of the solution space like how will I execute this product not problem part of the problem space which is what is it the customer is trying to do.

principles.text: Where a 'best version' exists, the job gets automated; where none exists (design, strategy, entertainment), AI augments but doesn't replace.
principles.quote: Any job where there is such a thing as a best version of that job will get automated. But there are many jobs where there's no such thing as a best.

principles.text: Frameworks rarely transplant; adopt one as 'better but wrong' and review what to change every two weeks.
principles.quote: this is probably better than what we're doing now, but it's also probably just 70% of what it needs to be.

principles.text: Aim for 'special' fit between your strengths and a slice of the market, not a unique selling proposition.
principles.quote: Special side of the market. Special. You're special in some way.
